- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.1) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates true price peaks in 30-day horizon; apply 1–3% upward bias if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.0–0.2) and price is rising, model lags; forecast should be 1–2 days ahead of actual trend.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.1–0.5), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before applying sentiment-weighted adjustment.
